details: The cryptocurrency market has seen a dramatic shift, with Bitcoin surging past $80,000 for the first time in months. This rally is largely attributed to the U.S. Treasury's announcement on August 19, 2026, to double its long-end debt buybacks, which subsequently weakened the U.S. dollar and lowered bond yields. This macroeconomic policy shift encouraged investors to move into risk assets, triggering a massive short squeeze that liquidated over $4 billion in bearish crypto positions. Strong inflows into spot Bitcoin ETFs also contributed significantly to the bullish momentum.
title: Bitcoin Reclaims $80K Amid Treasury Buybacks & Short Squeeze

details: Financial markets are keenly awaiting the release of the Core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) Price Index for July on August 26, 2026, which is the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge. Its outcome will heavily influence expectations for future interest rate decisions. Additionally, the annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, scheduled from August 27-29, 2026, will feature speeches from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, offering critical insights into the economic outlook and monetary policy. These events are expected to significantly impact both traditional and cryptocurrency markets.
title: US PCE Data & Jackson Hole to Dictate Market Direction

details: European Central Bank (ECB) Executive Board member Piero Cipollone has reiterated that the proposed digital euro will offer stronger privacy protections than standard bank transfers, asserting that the Eurosystem would not be able to link individuals to their transactions. The ECB is also making strides in developing a tokenized financial market to reduce fragmentation and diminish reliance on private settlement assets. The digital euro regulation received European Parliament approval in July 2026, with a potential launch slated for 2029.
title: ECB Details Digital Euro Privacy, Advances Tokenized Finance

details: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva stated that the global economy has withstood recent energy shocks better than anticipated, partly due to the growing tailwinds from artificial intelligence investments. The IMF considers AI a "macro-critical transition" capable of delivering substantial productivity gains and driving global economic growth beyond the U.S., marked by expanding investments in data centers and semiconductor manufacturing. This positive outlook on technological advancement could indirectly benefit risk assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: IMF Cites AI as Key Catalyst for Global Economic Growth

details: BlackRock has significantly reduced the minimum asset value required for qualified Bitcoin holders to convert their holdings into shares of its iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) from $25 million to $1 million, effective July 2026. This move broadens access to the in-kind conversion mechanism for a wider range of institutional and individual investors, allowing them to directly exchange Bitcoin for IBIT shares without needing to sell for cash first. This development signals increased institutional engagement and flexibility within regulated crypto investment products.
title: BlackRock Lowers IBIT Conversion Threshold to $1 Million

details: Better Mortgage and Coinbase have broadly launched their token-backed conforming mortgage product, now generally available to Coinbase One members. This innovative offering allows borrowers to pledge crypto assets as collateral while maintaining first-lien conformance to Fannie Mae guidelines. Additionally, eligible Coinbase One members can receive a 1% lender-funded closing cost credit. This initiative aims to expand homeownership access for crypto holders and further integrate digital assets into traditional financial services.
title: Coinbase and Better Launch Crypto-Backed Mortgages
